title: Serving runtime sync — hypothesis tracker & action prep (Julian)
content:
Context:
This is my prep/notebook for the weekly serving runtime sync. Mostly a scratchpad — will use to drive agenda and to capture quick actions during the meeting. Keep concise: bring up regressions, rollout blockers, console follow-ups, and one hypothesis to test this sprint.

Meeting details:
- Time: Wed 10:00am PT (30m)
- Attendees to nudge: Asha (runtime perf), Maya (console), Omar (infra), Priya (release), SRE on-call placeholder
- Goals: triage visible perf anomalies, align on canary rollback plan, capture 3 concrete action items, decide on experiment for KV cache tuning.

Proposed agenda (30m) — rough timings:
1) Quick surface (5m) — recent alerts + one-liners from each owner (Asha/Maya/Omar)
2) Regression deep-dive (10m) — 99th percentile token latency up on Model-X since 2026-03-07
3) Canary/rollback decision (5m) — current canary status and opt-out triggers
4) Hypothesis to test + experiment plan (5m) — KV cache TTL & batching thresholds
5) Action items & owners (5m) — confirm owners/due dates, add to INF board

Quick notes to surface before hand:
- Alerts last 48h: burst errors on region us-west2 between 02:00–04:00; error rate peaked 2.9% (threshold 0.5%). Logging attached in INF-2345.
- Latency: baseline 99p increased from 210ms -> 420ms for seq_len>1024 requests (Model-X v2.1.4). Possible correlation with new kernel selection heuristic rolled 2026-03-06.
- Console: customers report opaque error 502 message for batch requests; Maya looking at stack trace (PR 789).

Regression hypotheses (prioritized):
H1 (highest): Kernel selector change introduced a fallback path that disables fast attention kernels for some model partitions -> higher CPU work per token -> latency spike.
H2: Workload shift — higher proportion of long-seq requests exceeding pre-warm thresholds; batching logic not triggering due to TTL misconfiguration.
H3: Networking/transient infra causing increased retries and queueing, amplifying tail latency in bursts.

Metrics to pull before meeting (Julian action):
- 99/95/50 lat by model variant (v2.1.3 vs v2.1.4) last 7d
- Kernel selection histogram per shard for affected container images
- Retry counts, queue length, and CPU utilization across affected nodes
- Console error stack traces + request ids for three representative failures

Experiment plan (if we decide to test during sprint):
- Test: revert kernel-selector heuristic on one canary shard (dark launch) and compare 99p over 24h.
- Secondary test: increase KV cache TTL from 30s -> 120s for a small traffic slice (5%); measure token cost and 99p latency.
- Rollback criteria: if 99p improves by >=20% OR error rate drops below 0.7% for 24h, promote change; otherwise roll back.

Canary/rollback notes:
- Current canary: 10 nodes in us-west2 serving Model-X v2.1.4 with new selector. Traffic slice is 2.5%.
- Observation window: 6h window ended 2026-03-12 18:00 PT — small uplift noted but still under escalation threshold. Need to extend window.
- Manual rollback play: Priya to trigger image revert and restart canary nodes; allow 15 minutes for KV warm-up.

Action item tracker (populate during meeting):
- AI-1: Pull kernel selection histogram + attach to INF-2345 — owner: Julian Park — due: 2026-03-13
- AI-2: Reproduce 502 error locally with failing batch payloads, capture request ids, post in thread — owner: Maya Lin — due: 2026-03-14
- AI-3: Simulate increased long-seq traffic in staging, test batching TTL increase effect — owner: Asha Nair — due: 2026-03-18
- AI-4: If rollback condition met, Priya to run rollback playbook and notify SRE — owner: Priya Shah — due: trigger-based (note in INF-ops channel)
- AI-5: Add KV cache TTL experiment to Optimize suggestions doc and update cost estimate — owner: Omar Ruiz — due: 2026-03-16

Status of previous action items (quick):
- Prev AI: 'Add per-route 99p histogram to console' — in progress (Maya) — partial dashboard up, missing model split (blocked by PR 789)
- Prev AI: 'Investigate autoscaler flapping in us-west2' — closed (infra tweaked probe)

Parking lot / talking points if time:
- Longer-term: smarter kernel routing by seq-length prediction pre-scheduling (idea: runtime picks kernels based on traffic distribution sampled over 24h)
- Consider adding a rolling alert for kernel-fallback counts -> alert earlier than latency increase
- Customer-facing apology draft: if rollback needed, coordinate with CS for messaging (cc: Anya)

Notes-to-self (Julian):
- Keep the agenda tight — focus on 1 regression + 1 experiment.
- Push to create small reproducible test case for the 502 (makes triage quicker).
- If meeting runs long, split follow-ups into a separate "ops chase" session with SRE and infra.

Quick links (for in-meeting paste):
- INF-2345 (regression ticket)
- PR 789 (console stacktrace fix)
- Deploy playbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deploy+Playbook
